summary: Reviewed all new test classes added by WP-009 across test_supervisor.py and test_nodes.py, and cross-checked against the source implementations in supervisor.py and nodes/__init__.py.
Tests are well-structured, follow existing patterns, use appropriate mocking (pytest async, AsyncMock, plain-class stubs for inject_project_path compatibility), and cover all 11 acceptance criteria.

The _WPTool plain-class stub in TestPipelineResult._make_wp_tool is a deliberate and correctly documented design choice — MagicMock auto-creates _orig_ainvoke which silently breaks the inject_project_path wrapper.
Source code in nodes/__init__.py and supervisor.py is clean, minimal, and architecturally sound. No over-engineering, no unnecessary abstractions.

One non-blocking semantic issue identified: prev_result field in route log entries evaluates to 'PASS' on the very first iteration (when prev_wp_id is empty) because stage_success defaults to True. The correct value for 'no prior stage' should be an empty string. Does not affect routing; field is correctly populated in all meaningful iterations.

comments.note: supervisor.py: prev_result in route log entries is computed as 'PASS' if prev_success else ('FAIL' if prev_wp_id else ''). On the very first iteration, prev_wp_id='' and prev_success=True (state default), so prev_result='PASS' even though no prior stage ran. Semantically, the correct value when prev_wp_id is empty should always be ''. Consider swapping the condition to: '' if not prev_wp_id else ('PASS' if prev_success else 'FAIL'). Not a routing bug — all meaningful iterations set prev_wp_id correctly.

tests/test_supervisor.py: base_state() does not include run_start_ts, prev_wp_summaries, or wps_completed_this_run keys. Tests inject them ad-hoc per test method. A follow-up could add these optional fields to base_state() with None/[] defaults to make state shape explicit and aid future test writers.

tests/test_nodes.py TestPipelineResult: _make_wp_tool defines _WPTool as a nested class on every call. This is functionally correct, but the class-level 'name' attribute means all instances from any call share the same class. If future tests require different tool names from the same factory call, this pattern would need adjustment. Low risk given the test pattern.
No test covers test_route_prev_result_fail_when_stage_fails (TestEnrichedRouteEvents only tests the PASS branch). QA noted this gap; it remains as a low-priority coverage improvement.
